#1308. Baena and Pubill keep Spain perfect as ten-man Czechia are beaten 2-0 in Prague

Spain won 2-0 in Prague despite missing Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal, with Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena converting a penalty and Marc Pubill adding a late second. The win keeps the world champions perfect in Nations League Group A3 and leaves them needing only a draw against England on Sunday.

Spain beat ten-man Czechia 2-0 at the Letná Stadium in Prague on Thursday. They did it without three of their leading names. Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal were all missing. Atlético Madrid’s Álex Baena struck from the spot, and Marc Pubill added a late second. The world champions remain perfect in Group A3 before Sunday’s decider against England.

Conditions were raw. The game was played in 4°C, with light drizzle and humidity above 90%, the Spanish federation said. Czechia are coached by the Spaniard Santi Denia.

Chances were scarce before the break. Dean Huijsen’s header was Spain’s only open-play effort on target in the first half, and it was easily saved. The breakthrough came from the penalty spot. Lukáš Ambros was penalised for handball in the area. Baena’s powerful penalty beat goalkeeper Matěj Kovář.

Spain thought they had doubled the lead after half-time. VAR ruled out an effort by Yéremy Pino. The game was physical. Referee Nikola Dabanovic booked Pedro Porro in the 12th minute and Mikel Merino in the 69th. He then dismissed Krejčí, leaving the hosts a man down for the closing stages.

Spain made the extra man count deep into added time. Pubill won the ball back in Czechia’s half and rolled it into the bottom corner. That settled the contest. For Atlético followers, Baena’s goal was the night’s highlight. Fermín López, by contrast, is still waiting for his first Spain goal.

The victory was Spain’s 12th in a row and their fifth straight win in the Nations League. ESPN said it stretched their record unbeaten run in all competitions. Spain’s last defeat came against Colombia in March 2024. Czechia, meanwhile, have lost every Nations League game this season.

England kept pace on the same night. They beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley and sit three points behind Spain. That sets up a straight shoot-out for first place. A draw against England at the Metropolitano on Sunday will be enough for Spain to finish first in the group.

Terminamos los partidos a domicilio con pleno de victorias.

🇨🇿 🆚 🇪🇸 | 0-1 | 90+6’#VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/d8M1g03l6q

— Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol (@SEFutbol) November 12, 2026

Spain should also be stronger for that game. Yamal’s knee problem made Prague the first game he had missed for club or country this season. He had started all 20 previous matches, recording 17 goals and 13 assists. He will rejoin the squad for Sunday’s meeting with England.

#1307. Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 620–627 (2026) Cite this article

Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

#1306. Atlético Madrid buy 50% of Atlético FC, Guayaquil’s newly promoted Serie B champions

Atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season. The deal gives the Spanish club its first affiliate in South America before the Ecuadorian team steps up to Serie A in 2027.

The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.

The move had been signalled earlier in the year. On Friday 20 February 2026, Atlético said it would share sporting, institutional and commercial expertise with Atlético FC and might take a stake in the following months, El Comercio reported.

Regarded as Ecuador’s largest non-profit organisation, the Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil operates in all 24 of the country’s provinces.

The club’s route into Serie B was unusual. It took over the place of Atlético Vinotinto, which could not use it because its affiliate Vinotinto FC had been relegated. The team also changed its name from Atlético JBG to Atlético FC.

Promotion came on 15 October 2026 with a 1-0 win over Independiente Juniors. Fidel Martínez scored the goal. A week later, on Thursday 22 October, a 2-2 draw against Cuenca Juniors at the Estadio Alejandro Serrano sealed the title. That match was the ninth round of the promotion hexagonal.

Across the campaign the side scored 39 goals and conceded 21. It became the 37th different club to win Ecuador’s Serie B. The team is coached by Carlos Santamarina, who comes from Atlético’s academy.

The promotion also reshapes the city’s football map. Guayaquil will have four clubs in the 2027 Serie A: Atlético FC, Barcelona SC, Emelec and Guayaquil City.

Mexico and Canada already host clubs in the Madrid side’s network of linked teams, through Atlético de San Luis and Atlético Ottawa.

The investment builds on years of groundwork in Ecuador. Atlético and the Junta signed their original strategic agreement on Monday 24 July 2023 at the charity’s sports complex. Under that deal, the club’s academy would apply its coaching model to the Junta’s football division. At the time, that division served 2,500 children from vulnerable backgrounds.

In June 2026 the club put the number of young players at more than 14,000. That same month, chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín visited the academy’s Guayaquil base. With the Junta’s delegation, he watched an Atlético FC match and greeted Santamarina.

El Atlético Fútbol Club se une a la familia rojiblanca.

Nuestro club hace efectiva la adquisición del 50% del equipo ecuatoriano, que logró el ascenso a la Serie A en octubre de la mano del técnico de la Academia Carlos Santamarina.

— Atlético de Madrid (@Atleti) November 13, 2026

For Atlético, the stake creates a direct link between that youth work and a senior professional team.

The board holds its first meeting next week. It will elect a president proposed by Atlético and appoint a general manager.

#1305. O'Neill hails recalled midfield duo Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan after both net to help sink St Mirren

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

O’Neill said: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill said: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

‘I thought he did very well,’ said O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ said McLeish.

‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’

#1304. Tebas lists Real Madrid’s attacks on LaLiga a month after club demanded his resignation

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas says Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez said Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

Tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

The thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club said Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas said the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

The dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Tomás González-Martín sostiene en El Debate que un presidente de LaLiga no puede dedicarse a atacar a uno de sus socios. Para sostener su argumento, omite una parte esencial: las acusaciones que Florentino Pérez y los canales oficiales del Real Madrid…

— Javier Tebas Medrano (@Tebasjavier) November 15, 2026

Pérez now faces his members. Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. The only item at the extraordinary assembly is a proposal to ratify tennis player Rafael Nadal as a board member. The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.

#1303. McTominay and Anguissa: ‘Napoli can build momentum’ after 1-0 victory

Scott McTominay hopes Napoli can ‘get a bit of momentum going’ after his goal allowed them to beat Torino, while Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa insists ‘we can climb back up the table.’

It was a difficult match for the Partenopei, who struggled to break Toro down and also ran a risk when Ronaldo Mandragora thumped the crossbar from distance.

McTominay finally broke the deadlock with a strike from the edge of the area, set up for him by Noa Lang after a defensive run to win back the ball, turning it into an attacking situation.

The Scotland international has a real history against Torino, scoring four goals past them in only three meetings.

“In football it’s about the next game, and the next game, you have to do your best. We have a team that wants to work, wants to push, and we want to win more games,” McTominay told Sky Sport Italia.

Allegri turned to his bench after the goal and said: ‘See, they score when they smile, I told them to smile more.’

“I am feeling much better,” smiled McTominay.

“It’s an important goal, but more importantly we won, we had to win. I’m happy for the fans, we need to get a bit of momentum going, keep winning.”

Now there is a trip to Manchester City in the Champions League, which will feel like a derby for former Manchester United midfielder McTominay.

“A great game, we’ll recover now and then think about it from tomorrow.”

There had been some changes and tactical experiments, moving to a 3-5-2 formation, but Antonio Vergara limped off after just 11 minutes and is now expected to miss Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Manchester City.

Kevin De Bruyne had initially been rested with that in mind too, but had to come on to replace Vergara, meaning extra fatigue on 35-year-old legs.

“When you work as a team, it becomes easier for everyone,” added Anguissa.

“We know what Scott can do, we’re happy he scored and these are three very important points. We have to keep working together, it is the only way to get out of this situation. We are very concentrated and know what we need to do.

“It is important to think positive, take it one game at a time. I have faith, and I feel that this team can do anything. There’s a long way to go this season, we can climb back up the table.”

#1302. Fan who racially abused Mbappé at Oviedo given suspended 11-month prison sentence

A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

The Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

The abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

The man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid said in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

The fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

The case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

The ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

The Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

For Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

Comunicado Oficial.https://t.co/wiUVApFn17

— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 17, 2026

The pattern points to clubs and the league pursuing racist abuse through the criminal courts rather than leaving it to stadium sanctions alone. In the Oviedo case, the combination of a league complaint and lip-reading evidence was decisive.

Real Madrid is now acting as private prosecutor in other cases involving similar incidents against its players.

#1301. Supreme Court makes CVC vote annulment final, but LaLiga’s December deal approval stands

Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

Spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly announced a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

Real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

LaLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga said the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

The deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A new company set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

That leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.

Comunicado Oficial.https://t.co/CMGkLNsGuT

— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 17, 2026

The fight over the December agreements is not over either. Real Madrid has taken that ruling to the Supreme Court, which has not yet decided whether to admit the appeal.

#1300. Allegri: ‘Napoli needed to smile for a goal, McTominay and De Bruyne switched role’

Max Allegri explains the tactical tweaks he made for Scott McTominay and Kevin De Bruyne during Napoli’s 1-0 win over Torino, not to mention his advice. ‘Try smiling and we might get a goal.’

The Partenopei struggled to get the better of Torino at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, and were rescued by the woodwork when Rolando Mandragora’s screamer surprised Vanja Milinkovic-Savic just before half-time.

However, McTominay got the only goal of the game when Noa Lang turned a defensive run into an attacking one, setting up the Scotland international on the edge of the area.

It was noted on the touchline that after the goal, Allegri turned to his bench and said this was because he had told the players to smile more.

“The mood wasn’t right because we had so many chances, I told them at half-time to try smiling and we might get a goal,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

“They did really well to win this game, while suffering against a strong opponent. Perhaps it is positive that we won under pressure, but we also should’ve done better controlling the tempo, moving the ball from one side to the other.

“The lads did very well in defending on set plays and corner kicks.”

It came at a cost, as Napoli’s injury crisis intensified further with Antonio Vergara limping off just 11 minutes into the game, meaning there was barely any rest for De Bruyne ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League trip to Manchester City.

At first, De Bruyne was in the more advanced role behind Rasmus Hojlund, but after a few minutes Allegri dropped the Belgium international deeper and put McTominay there instead.

“The fun thing about this job is finding solutions. I am starting to get to know these players, I thought De Bruyne could do better as a support for the striker, but in this situation, McTominay was more useful,” explained the coach.

“I just told McTominay not to be already in the position right behind Hojlund, but to run into that space, as it would make him harder to mark. If he is already there and not mobile, then obviously he’s going to be easier to control, but he started to move between the lines and did better.

“I think Hojlund had a good game, he worked for the team. In football, sometimes things go well in one situation, then go badly in another. Today we finally managed to defend with more determination and grit, but then didn’t score as many as before.

“Hojlund scored on international duty last week, he is a very useful player for us.”

Allegri has made history, becoming the first ever coach to amass 1,100 Serie A points, but now he faces a difficult Champions League trip to Manchester City on Tuesday.

“We need to be realistic, because as I said when the fixture list was first drawn up, our Champions League qualification would be decided in the final three matches,” said the coach.

“On Tuesday we need a good performance, try to get a result, but also know that we’ve got to sort our Serie A position first.”

#1299. Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

#1298. Ten-man Tenerife beat Badajoz 5-2 in Copa del Rey tie postponed after De Miguel’s death

Tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

The Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

Tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

This was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

Cervera’s side return to league duty at home to Mallorca in Segunda División on Saturday 21 November. Badajoz travel to Recreativo Huelva in Segunda División RFEF Group 4 on Sunday 22 November.

The second round will feature 56 teams in 28 one-off ties. The lower-division side hosts if its ground meets federation standards. The draw was put back because of the postponed first-round matches. The Ciudad del Fútbol in Las Rozas, Madrid, home of the federation, is the venue for it.

#1297. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.

Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.

Arsenal get the game under way, playing in their navy away kit.

The rain continues to lash down. Jurgen Klopp, Germany’s manager, is in the stands having a flim-flam with Rafael Benitez, who has dashed to Bavaria from Anfield where he watched Liverpool vs Villarreal last night.

It seems like Vincent Kompany may have taken a leaf out of Thomas Tuchel’s tactical book. Kompany appears to have done the same here with Davies, usually a left-back, starting as a winger.

A fascinating aspect of tonight’s game is how Konsa and Gabriel decide to deal with him. Will Arsenal commit to a man-to-man press, with the centre-backs following Kane well beyond the halfway line, or preserve a more zonal approach?

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Will the substitutes again make the difference for Arsenal tonight? In each of their last three league victories, they have won because of goals scored by substitutes. Over the last year or so, this has become a real strength.

Karl had been expected to replace Olise on the right, but Kompany looks to have stiffened up his midfield by starting Pavlovic, Laimer and Bischof. It will be interesting to see how Saibari and Kane dovetail, two stick-on strikers. It is not Bayern’s strongest team, with Luis Diaz also on the bench.

Bayern Munich starting XI: Neuer, Stanisic, Kim Minjae, Upamecano, Davies, Pavlovic, Laimer, Bischof, Gnabry, Saibari, Kane

There was little doubt that Arteta would view this game as one that suits Jurrien Timber rather than Ben White. Arsenal’s manager has changed tack by starting Calafiori, who was rested for Arsenal’s first two Champions League games, but Bayern at the Allianz is a significant step up in grade. Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1296. Real Madrid tie Tchouaméni and Güler to 2032 contracts within 24 hours

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing its core midfield for years to come.

Real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

Both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

His standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The new contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

Güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His new salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

The two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

The club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The new deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

🚨🤍 Aurelien Tchouameni has signed new long term deal at Real Madrid until June 2032. pic.twitter.com/13BtcLyubP

— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 19, 2026

Tchouaméni has not been fully clear of fitness concerns this month. Earlier in November he left the France squad with a muscle problem. He was back in training with the Madrid squad on the day his renewal was announced.

Real Madrid host Celta at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday 21 November at 21:00 in LaLiga matchday 13. PSV then visit for a Champions League game on Tuesday 24 November.

#1294. Roberto Fernández goal gives Eder Sarabia first Espanyol win at San Mamés

Espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

The win was Eder Sarabia’s first in charge of Espanyol. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

His appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win over Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

The first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

Sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

In front of goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño, who kept a clean sheet, defender O. El Hilali was rated 7.16.

The result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

Athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14

— Athletic Club (@Athletic_en) November 20, 2026

Before kick-off, San Mamés paid tribute to Elene Gurtubay and Daniela Agote, who won the Under-20 World Cup.

After 12 matches, Terzić’s side have 16 points. Their recent run reads one draw, two wins and one defeat in the league before Friday’s loss. Real Sociedad sit fifth on 22 points.

Athletic travel to bottom side Malaga on Saturday 28 November. Espanyol host Getafe on Monday 30 November.

#1293. Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

Symbols indicate data sources, including sites with (1) both eddy-covariance flux and phenocam observations (n = 3; green stars); (2) eddy-covariance flux only (n = 1; blue star); (3) phenocam observations only (n = 2; yellow stars); (4) litterfall observations (n = 47; red triangles); (5) inventory plots (n = 289; purple circles); and (6) very high-resolution Google Earth image locations (n = 16; 0.5-m spatial resolution, each covering a 2 km × 2 km area; blue squares). Site information, including location, data type, and observation period, is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The map was created using ArcGIS Pro with the Esri World Ocean Base basemap. Basemap sources: Esri, Garmin, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC and other contributors.

Panels a-e compare the temporal dynamics of ecosystem-scale deciduousness fraction from Sentinel-2 (blue line) with the fraction of leafless tree crowns visually assessed from phenocam images (black line). The Sentinel-2 deciduousness fraction is calculated as the mean value within a 500 m × 500 m area centred on each phenocam site, while the phenocam typically covers an area of approximately 100 m × 100 m. Panel f shows the relationship between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness and the corresponding deciduousness derived from phenocam observations across five sites (n = 60 paired site-month observations). The solid line indicates an ordinary least-squares linear regression, with statistical significance assessed using a two-sided test (p = 6.17 × 10−22).

a, Relationship between standardized monthly litterfall and standardized satellite-derived deciduousness across annual cycles at 47 Amazonian sites (n = 559 pooled site-month observations). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear regression across all pooled data, and the inset boxplot summarizes the site-level distribution of correlation coefficients (r, n = 47 sites). b, Relationship between satellite-derived deciduousness amplitude and the ground-derived proportion of deciduous tree species across the Amazon basin. Grey circles represent raw plot-to-pixel observations (n = 289 plots). The red line shows the ordinary least-squares linear fit to the raw observations, and the shaded band indicates the 95% confidence interval of the fitted mean relationship. The dashed grey line indicates the 1:1 relationship. For a and b, statistical significance of the regression slopes was assessed using two-sided tests (a, p = 2.52 × 10−141; b, p = 7.24 × 10−28). The p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. c, Patch-level comparison of deciduousness derived from Sentinel-2 (y-axis) against that derived from closely date-matched, high-resolution Google Earth imagery (GEI; x-axis) via image-specific Random Forest classification and pooled across all 16 validation scenes. Each dot represents a 100-m × 100-m aggregated patch (n = 6058 patches), and the dashed black line marks the 1:1 relationship. d, e, Scene-level distributions of correlation coefficients (r; d) and root-mean-square errors (RMSE; e) calculated separately for each of the 16 GEI validation scenes. Grey dots represent individual scenes. In all boxplots, the centre line indicates the median, the box bounds the interquartile range (IQR), and the whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR.

a, c, e, g, Spatial maps of evergreen forest cover (a), MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields tree cover (c), EVI amplitude (e) and VOD amplitude (g). Inset histograms show the basin-wide frequency distribution of each metric. b, d, f, h, Corresponding pixel-level relationships between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness amplitude and the four reference metrics. Hexbin colour indicates observation density, and dashed lines indicate least-squares linear regressions. Sample sizes (b, d, f, h) were n = 227,612, 227,612, 226,942 and 221,884 valid paired forest pixels, reflecting product-specific data availability. All two-sided tests gave p < 10−300. Correlation coefficients (r) and regression equations are shown in each panel.

Panels a-h show how each variable affects deciduousness–greenness asynchrony, with positive SHAP values (>0) indicating a positive effect and negative SHAP values (<0) indicating a negative effect. The black line in each panel represents a fitted line, summarizing the central tendency of the data points.

Bar charts show the proportional influence of hydroclimate, soil, and light for the entire basin (a), Southern Amazon (b), Guiana Shield (c), and Everwet Amazon (d).

a-c, Spatial patterns of model-performance gain, expressed as the change in the correlation coefficient (Δr) between the GPP seasonality simulated by LD-LUE and that simulated by each corresponding conventional LUE model, with both evaluated against satellite SIF. Results are shown for the EC-LUE (a), two-leaf EC-LUE (TL-EC-LUE; b) and MODIS-LUE (c). Positive Δr indicates better agreement of LD-LUE with satellite SIF relative to its conventional counterpart. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0.

a-l, Comparisons of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites (K34, K67, CAX, and RJA). Rows correspond to the three core LUE formulations: EC-LUE (a-d), TL-EC-LUE (e-h), and MODIS-LUE (i–l). Black dashed lines with open circles represent EC observations. Coloured lines with open markers represent conventional baselines driven by various vegetation inputs (e.g., NDVI, EVI, kNDVI, MODIS-LAI), whereas solid red lines with filled markers denote the LD-LUE models. m, n, Dumbbell plots showing site-level performance and across-site mean in terms of the temporal correlation coefficient (r) (m) and RMSE (n). Open symbols denote the conventional baselines, whereas the corresponding filled symbols denote the LD-LUE models. The vertical lines connecting each pair indicate the magnitude and direction of performance changes following incorporation of the LD module. Symbol colours distinguish the baseline input configurations, and symbol shapes indicate the underlying model formulations (circles, EC-LUE; triangles, TL-EC-LUE; squares, MODIS-LUE).

a-d, Spatial distribution of model performance gain, expressed as Δr, for EC-LUE (a), TL-EC-LUE (b), MODIS-LUE (c), and mean Δr across the three models (d). Δr is calculated as the difference in the correlation coefficient between satellite SIF and the GPP seasonality simulated by the LD-LUE model (that incorporates both satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs and leaf demography) and that simulated by the corresponding baseline model (which includes only satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs). Positive values indicate improved seasonal agreement with SIF after incorporating leaf-age-dependent physiological dynamics, whereas negative values indicate reduced agreement. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0. e, Stacked bar chart showing the proportional breakdown of pixels with improved (red) and degraded (blue) Δr averaged across the three models, for each ecoregion (Southern Amazon, Guiana Shield, and Everwet Amazon) and the entire Amazon basin.

a-d, Comparison of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites: K34 (a), K67 (b), CAX (c), and RJA (d). Red lines with triangles represent the full leaf-demography-enabled model (LD-LUE), while blue lines with squares represent the baseline model (LAIdec-LUE), which uses the same deciduousness-derived LAI but assumes a seasonally fixed photosynthetic capacity. Black dashed lines with open circles indicate the EC-derived GPP observations. Shaded bands indicate ±1 standard error of the mean (SEM; n = 3 LUE formulations per ensemble). e-g, Quantitative assessment of model performance gains across the four sites, comparing LD-LUE (red bars) and LAIdec-LUE (blue bars) in terms of correlation coefficient (r; e), root mean square error (RMSE; f), and amplitude ratio (g). The amplitude ratio in (g) is calculated relative to the observed seasonal amplitude, with the horizontal dashed line at 1.0 indicating perfect agreement.

#1292. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Thirty-one years ago, Patrick Kluivert scored against AC Milan in Europe. If his son Justin’s eighth-minute penalty will not receive the acclaim of Patrick’s winner for Ajax in the 1995 Champions League final, the goal will be etched in Bournemouth’s hearts.

After Evanilson’s header from a corner struck Koni De Winter’s hand, a VAR review led to Bournemouth being awarded a penalty. Kluivert eyed up Mike Maignan, and waited for the goalkeeper to dive before nonchalantly stroking the ball into the unguarded left corner.

Bournemouth lead against AC Milan in a European competition! 🍒 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1BQt3wKSr9

And so Bournemouth were beating AC Milan, a scenario that would have seemed unfathomable for vast swathes of these two clubs’ existence. Even more extraordinary was how deserved the goal was: both Kluivert and Evanilson had already spurned opportunities, with Milan seeming overwhelmed by Bournemouth’s intensity.

Watching his side lack any coherence in their passing, Ruben Amorim rapidly came to look as ghoulish as in his last days at Old Trafford. Or, indeed, Michael Carrick in Como 24 hours earlier.

Amorim swiftly had cause to become more irate. Just as Milan had threatened to regain a semblance of control, Maignan inexplicably pushed Tyler Adams in the face when Bournemouth had a corner. VAR had no reason to give Maignan a reprieve from his red card, and Bournemouth’s ensuing penalty.

AC Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan is shown a straight red for a push to the face of Tyler Adams 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/0IkySebkkv

Kluivert has scored all eight penalties in his professional career. But Lorenzo Torriani, the substitute goalkeeper, instead had to face Marcus Tavernier, who rolled the ball to the keeper’s right corner. Bournemouth were 2-0 and a man up within 32 minutes; AC Milan were collapsing like the Dow Jones Industrial Average in 1929.

Another Bournemouth penalty, another Bournemouth goal. Marcus Tavernier gives the Cherries a 2-0 lead 🤩 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/kRAoUTQVYl

By the last throes of this mismatch, fans gleefully sang “We want four”. They were denied, but no matter: for Bournemouth fans, this was a magnificently surreal evening on the south coast.

A historic evening for Bournemouth ends in a dominant 3-0 victory over 10-man Milan. First-half penalties from Kluivert and Tavernier, combined with Maignan’s foolish red card, left Milan with an impossible mountain to climb. Adli’s magical free kick added some serious gloss to the scoreline late on. The seven-time European champions didn’t record a shot on target as Amorim endured an unhappy return to England. Bournemouth have taken maximum points from their opening three Europa League games and continue their 100% winning record in the competition.
